# iBio Announces New Preclinical Data Across Obesity and Cardiometabolic Portfolio at Multiple Scientific Conferences


November 16, 2026 4:30pm EST


*ObesityWeek 2026 data from obese non-human primates showed sustained Activin E suppression and a 2.3% vehicle-adjusted reduction in body weight from baseline with IBIO-610 at week 28.*


*Amylin program data demonstrating reduced food intake in rats to be presented at PEGS Europe and the Amylin-Based Therapeutics Summit*


*Together, the findings highlight the potential of iBio’s antibody discovery platform to generate highly specific candidates against distinct targets*


SAN DIEGO, Nov. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- iBio, Inc. (NASDAQ: IBIO), a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing long-acting antibody therapeutics for obesity, cardiometabolic and cardiopulmonary diseases, today announced extended preclinical data from a non-human primate (NHP) study of IBIO-610, potentially a first-in-class Activin E antibody candidate, presented at ObesityWeek 2026, as well as preclinical data from its amylin program to be presented at PEGS Europe 2026 and the Amylin-Based Therapeutics Summit.


“These data demonstrate the power of our AI-enabled antibody discovery platform to generate potent, highly specific molecules against challenging targets,” said Martin Brenner, DVM, Ph.D., chief executive officer and chief scientific officer of iBio. “The sustained effects observed in our NHP study strengthen our belief in IBIO-610’s potential to offer a differentiated approach to long-term weight management. Durable Activin E suppression, reductions in fat mass while generally maintaining lean mass, and the newly observed reduction in body weight provide a more comprehensive perspective of how this approach may improve the quality of weight loss. Beyond IBIO-610, our amylin program has taken an important step forward, demonstrating high selectivity for amylin receptors and reduced food intake in a preclinical model. We believe this selective approach has the potential to improve the balance of efficacy and tolerability and look forward to evaluating it in further studies. By pursuing multiple distinct mechanisms, we have the opportunity to build a complementary portfolio of medicines with the potential to extend the cardiometabolic benefits of weight loss beyond current therapies.”


**IBIO-610 Activin E Data presented at ObesityWeek 2026**
The new data for iBio’s long-acting Activin E-targeting antibody, IBIO-610, builds on previously reported findings from an obese NHP study, extending observations through 28 weeks.


The study included obese NHPs receiving IBIO-610 (n=5) or vehicle (n=6). IBIO-610 was initially administered every eight weeks, followed by more frequent dosing and a dose-free period.


**Key findings:**


- IBIO-610 reduced weight gain despite continued high-fat feeding, with body weight beginning to diverge from the vehicle group around Week 18 and reaching a 2.3% difference by Week 28.


- At Week 24, total body fat was 9.6% lower, abdominal subcutaneous fat 16.6% lower, and visceral fat 10.96% lower compared with vehicle, while lean mass was generally maintained.


- Near-complete suppression of active Activin E was observed through week 28.


These findings build on previously reported[data](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=e7DSMLGT733yqzz3QsV1kQct_eTW6cmOpOez3rlKmRiYWfprUA7ITvCNV6_RVR2oOcufR6F6D3uUjHv-n0Hn56T_k9-Z3tJtPFRFTyfJmVvZclCMG-GVS3eYxwpkY-yNm6NAi_lM7NVDQ3bzTUyEmQQ8qKjgHCZXYrKF8SapBPQvg6dx9W0KrvmZjyY1cduQ_-4S36n08n_IAlVHJLXSXuRuLHAzWe0D30UluGpdW1GHK3AQ6y-FftHhxAA144uypl_Qw1qm6tGY9XGUp9cmDsDkgaoNxAeta-xeNqp58AE2iDoeVxSvULAL5bOPPbUJ) from the NHP study and further support IBIO-610’s potential to promote fat-selective effects while maintaining lean mass.


**Amylin Program Data to Be Presented at PEGS Europe and the Amylin-Based Therapeutics Summit**


iBio’s amylin program combines a receptor-targeting antibody with a fused peptide agonist and demonstrated highly selective activation of amylin receptors 1 and 3. The findings highlight the platform’s ability to generate highly specific antibodies against challenging targets and support the development of a potential long-acting amylin therapeutic.


**Key findings:**


- In vitro, iBio’s antibody-peptide fusion selectively bound and activated amylin receptors 1 and 3, with minimal binding to or activation of the calcitonin receptor alone.


- In a single-dose study in lean rats, the rats dosed with iBio’s selective amylin receptor agonist had reduced food intake over 24 hours compared with vehicle.


iBio plans to advance selective amylin receptor agonists into further preclinical studies in diet-induced obesity models.
